html:
The Pitta Pitta are an Aboriginal Australian people of western Queensland, around today's town of Boulia on the Burke River. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their country is part of the Channel Country, where rivers spread into many braided channels after rain and feed the Lake Eyre basin. Trade routes for pituri, a native tobacco, and for ochre passed through the region. In the 1890s the doctor and ethnographer Walter Roth, working at Boulia, recorded the Pitta Pitta language and customs in detail, so they are among the better described peoples of the area. Neighbours on the map include the Wangkamana, the Mithaka and the Yalarrnga. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
